questionText:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions.
X Itd. Issued 30,000 shares to the public having Face value 100 at 10%
premium. Money is receivable as follows:
Application = 40 (including premium)
Allotment=45
 

First and Final call = Remaining amount
The public applied for 50,000 shares. The company rejected application for
10,000 shares and made a pro rata allotment to the rest of the applicants. A
shareholder applying for 400 shares, didn't pay the allotment and call
money and his allotted shares were forfeited by the company. Later, the
forfeited shares were reissued at 80 each as fully paid.
The amount of Security Premium Reserve shown under the sub-head
"Reserves and Surplus" will be:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Share Capital.
Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

detailedSolution:

For Share Capital (Company Accounts: Accounting for Share and Debenture Capital):
1. Allotted shares: 400 * (3/4) = 300 shares.
2. Excess application money: (400 - 300) * 40 = Rs. 4,000.
3. Allotment arrears: (300 * 45) - 4,000 = Rs. 9,500.
4. Call arrears: 300 * 25 = Rs. 7,500.
5. Total credited to Calls-in-Arrears = 9,500 + 7,500 = Rs. 17,000.
6. Matches Option C.

Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.

questionText:
The following are the features of the fluctuating capital method by which
the capital accounts of partners can be maintained.
(A) Under the fluctuating capital method, only one account, i.e. capital
account is maintained for each partner.
(B) All the adjustments such as share of profit and loss, interest on capital,
drawings, interest on drawings, etc. are recorded directly in the capital
accounts of the partners.
(C) the capital of the partners shall remain fixed unless additional capital is
introduced or a part of the capital is withdrawn as per the agreement
between the partners.
(D) The capital account may sometimes show a debit balance.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Assumed both statements were correct.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies that both statements contain factual errors.

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to recognize error in Statement II.

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to recognize error in Statement I.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Detailed Solution:
1. Statement (A): Only one capital account is maintained per partner. True for fluctuating method.
2. Statement (B): All adjustments (profits, drawings, interest) are posted directly to capital. True for fluctuating method.
3. Statement (C): 'Capitals remain fixed unless additional capital is introduced or withdrawn.' This defines the FIXED method, NOT fluctuating.
4. Statement (D): Capital account may sometimes show a debit balance. True for fluctuating method.
5. Therefore, statements (A), (B), and (D) only are features of the fluctuating capital method.
Hence, option (A) is correct.
Hence, option (B) is correct.

List-II

(CHARACTERISTICS)
(A) unlimited company
(i) liability arises only in the event of winding
up
(B) one person company
(II) limits the number of members to 200
C) private company
(III) paid up capital is not more than 50 lakhs
(D) company limited by
guarantee.
(IV) creditors can claim their dues from the
members.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
1. (A) Unlimited company: Members have unlimited personal liability, so creditors can claim directly -> (IV).
2. (B) One Person Company: Formerly restricted to paid-up capital of not more than Rs. 50 lakhs (under Rule 3) -> (III).
3. (C) Private company: Under Section 2(68), limits number of members to 200 -> (II).
4. (D) Company limited by guarantee: Member liability arises strictly in the event of winding up -> (I).
5. Matching combination: (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I).
Hence, option (C) is the correct match.

1. (A) Unlimited company: Members have unlimited personal liability, so creditors can claim directly -> (IV).
2. (B) One Person Company: Formerly restricted to paid-up capital of not more than Rs. 50 lakhs (under Rule 3) -> (III).
3. (C) Private company: Under Section 2(68), limits number of members to 200 -> (II).
4. (D) Company limited by guarantee: Member liability arises strictly in the event of winding up -> (I).
5. Matching combination: (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I).
Hence, option (C) is the correct match.

topic: Forfeiture and Reissue of Shares: Transfer to Capital Reserve
questionText: Company Apex #11 forfeited 400 shares of Rs. 10 each on which Rs. 7 per share was received. 200 of these shares were reissued as fully paid-up at Rs. 8 per share. What amount is transferred to Capital Reserve Account?

options.text: Share Forfeiture Dr. Rs. 1,400 to Capital Reserve A/c Rs. 1,400
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Share Forfeiture Dr. Rs. 1,000 to Capital Reserve A/c Rs. 1,000
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT concept for Forfeiture and Reissue of Shares: Transfer to Capital Reserve.

options.text: Share Forfeiture Dr. Rs. 400 to Capital Reserve A/c Rs. 400
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Share Forfeiture Dr. Rs. 2,800 to Capital Reserve A/c Rs. 2,800
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Company Accounts: Accounting for Share and Debenture Capital (Forfeiture and Reissue of Shares: Transfer to Capital Reserve):
Share Forfeiture Dr. Rs. 1,000 to Capital Reserve A/c Rs. 1,000

Detailed Context:
1. Forfeited amount on 400 shares = 400 x Rs. 7 = Rs. 2,800.
2. Forfeited amount proportional to 200 reissued shares = 200 x Rs. 7 = Rs. 1,400.
3. Discount allowed on reissue = 200 x (Rs. 10 - Rs. 8) = Rs. 400.
4. Net gain transferred to Capital Reserve = Rs. 1,400 - Rs. 400 = Rs. 1,000.
Hence Option A is correct.

Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.
